title.narrative: UN Action against Conflict-Related Sexual Violence Ukraine joint project

description.narrative: Support to the initiative "Strengthening national and community-based Conflict-Related Sexual Violence (CRSV) prevention and response mechanisms in Ukraine through a survivor-centered multi-sectoral approach," coordinated via the UN Action Secretariat in the Office of the Special Representative of the Secretary-General on Sexual Violence in Conflict, and implemented in Ukraine by UNFPA, UNODC, UNDP, IOM, UN Women, and WHO. The overall objective of this project is that the rights and needs of survivors of CRSV in Ukraine are properly addressed through an improved system-wide response. The objective is to be ensured through enhanced awareness, knowledge, capacity and technical expertise of Ukrainian institutions working on CRSV, including the Government of Ukraine, health care system, judiciary, prosecution, police, academia and civil society, as well as increased access to multi-sectoral assistance for survivors, reduced risks, an improved framework for gender-sensitive justice and reparations, and strengthened coordination between key international and national actors. The project particularly enhances the capacities of women-led organizations (WLOs), survivors’ networks and organizations working directly with survivors of CRSV. By doing so, women’s role in peacebuilding and recovery processes is enhanced. Among its proposed activities, the project forees training for national actors, advocacy, awareness-raising, conducting of two cycles of rehabilitation programmes for female survivors of CRSV, but will also address the needs of male survivors of CRSV through specialized training on Clinical Management of Rape (CMR) for service providers. The initiative has a special geographical focus on the areas near the frontline and locations hosting large caseloads of IDPs.
